title: Redrawing the Org Chart Around Agents
excerpt: Most companies are still asking how many people to cut. The leaders already stopped asking that question. A layoff removes cost. A reorg changes shape.

title: Prove It First, Then Cut
excerpt: 128,000 tech workers lost their jobs this year, nearly half cut because of AI. But 55% of the companies that did it already regret it. Most cut first and deployed second.

title: The Vendor Is Now the Consultant
excerpt: This week, OpenAI launched a $4 billion consulting firm. The company that builds the model now sells you the team that installs it. The architect profits from the architecture.

title: On-Prem AI Is Now Required
excerpt: The cloud was the default for AI. That default is shifting. 85% of enterprises plan to move AI workloads on-premises within two years. The reasons are mathematical, legal, and operational.

title: The Cost of AI Politeness
excerpt: "Thank you." Two tokens. Zero value. And your company just paid for it. Every token you send is a billing event, and every billing event reprocesses the full conversation.

title: The CUDA Moat Cracked
excerpt: Jensen Huang warned on April 15 that DeepSeek on Huawei chips would be horrible. Eight days later, DeepSeek shipped V4 on Huawei Ascend — trained entirely outside NVIDIA's ecosystem.

title: The Frontier Pileup
excerpt: GPT-5.5. DeepSeek V4. Tencent Hy3. Three frontier models in 48 hours, separated by single-digit percentage points. The capability gap closed. The trust gap did not. The price gap widened.

title: The Agent Layer Goes Live
excerpt: Four companies shipped production-grade agent platforms in one week: Anthropic, Microsoft, OpenAI, and xAI. An agent is not a feature inside your software. An agent is the employee that uses the software.

title: What Is Apache 2.0 and Why It Matters
excerpt: Apache 2.0 is the gold standard of open source licensing. Google just released Gemma 4 under it — the most permissive license a frontier-class model family has ever shipped under.

title: The Managed LLM Era
excerpt: For every company that spent two years saying "we cannot use AI because our data cannot leave the building" — that constraint just met its answer. Gemma 4 runs locally, under Apache 2.0.

title: Cybersecurity Changed This Week
excerpt: Anthropic built Claude Mythos Preview. It found a 27-year-old vulnerability in OpenBSD that every human researcher and every automated tool missed. Then Anthropic did something unprecedented: they refused to release it.

title: Open Source AI Just Became Enterprise-Ready
excerpt: Google released Gemma 4 — Apache 2.0, one architecture from phone to data center, native multimodality. The story is not the benchmarks. It is what landed in a single release.

title: Welcome — Why I’m Writing Publicly
excerpt: A short note on what to expect from this space: AI transformation field notes, executive perspective on the rate of change, and lessons from running production AI workloads.

title: AI Is the New Cloud
excerpt: "AI" is the new "cloud" — a useful category but almost useless as a plan. Under the umbrella are at least a dozen distinct technologies, each with its own cost curve and failure modes.

title: Your Product Roadmap Is Already Wrong
excerpt: AI has changed all of the timelines, budgets and features — most executives just don't know it yet. The transition is not in front of you. It is behind you.
